Activate weft in a project's documents

Source: R/setup.R
use_setup.Rd

Sets up the activation of weft (rule 9.2): the project .Rprofile that calls weft_setup() in every knit, or the same call in each document's front matter, together with the _weft.yml that records the weft version. It says what it will write before it writes anything, and running it again changes nothing. suppressMessages() silences it.

Usage

use_setup(path = ".", route = c("auto", "rprofile", "front-matter"))

Arguments

path

A folder or one document. Default: the current folder.

route

"auto", "rprofile" or "front-matter".

Value

The paths written, relative to the root, invisibly (character() when nothing changed).

Details

path is a folder or one .qmd, .Rmd or .rmd file. A folder in a Quarto project (a _quarto.yml here or above it) is set up at the project root. The route is "rprofile" in a Quarto project and "front-matter" otherwise, unless you choose.

It writes:

  • _weft.yml, when there is none (a comment and weft_version:), or the weft_version: line appended to one that lacks it. An existing line is left as it is.

  • route "rprofile": the .Rprofile at the project root. A new file sources ~/.Rprofile first, because R reads one profile only; an existing file gains a comment and the activation line after its last line (after source("renv/activate.R"), so weft is found in renv's library). A file that already calls weft::weft_setup() is kept.

  • route "front-matter": knitr: opts_knit: weft: !expr weft::weft_setup() in each document's front matter.

  • engine: knitr in each .qmd that has no engine: or jupyter: key and is not another engine's alone, except files and folders whose names start with _ or . (includes). A page of another engine's chunks alone gains the line only when it holds an R construct: an R value (`r x`{.num}) or a span whose governor is outside the grammar of the filter. A page of named values (`depth`{.num}) and spans of that grammar, or with no construct, stays as it is.

  • for an .Rmd outside a Quarto project, weft.lua, weft-check.lua, weft-output.lua and the folder weftlib/ beside the document (weft's own files: kept when identical, replaced when they differ) and, under each format of output:, pandoc_args: ["--lua-filter", "weft.lua", "--lua-filter", "weft-check.lua", "--lua-filter", "weft-output.lua"]. A document set up before named values, which names only weft-check.lua, gets weft.lua named before it; one set up before the rendered-output check gets weft-output.lua named last.

Front matter is edited as text and checked by parsing it again. When an edit cannot be made safely (flow-style knitr: or pandoc_args, a YAML anchor, another weft: value under opts_knit), or a file's place holds a folder or a symbolic link, nothing is written, and the error prints the lines to add by hand.

Examples

dir <- tempfile("weft-example")
dir.create(dir)
writeLines("", file.path(dir, "_weft.yml"))
writeLines(c(
  "---",
  "title: Survey",
  "---",
  "",
  "We visited 14 sites.",
  "",
  "```{r}",
  "n_high <- 3",
  "```",
  "",
  "[No site | One site | # sites]{n=n_high} read high."
), file.path(dir, "survey.Rmd"))
use_setup(dir)
#> weft will write, under /tmp/RtmpB7FqLJ/weft-example1a0013c1eb1a:
#>   _weft.yml  (edit: adds the weft_version line)
#>   survey.Rmd  (edit: adds the weft setup line and names the weft-check filter)
#>   weft-check.lua  (new: the weft-check filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weft-output.lua  (new: the rendered-output check for rmarkdown)
#>   weft.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weftlib/cond.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weftlib/config.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weftlib/ledger.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weftlib/lines.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weftlib/num.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weftlib/report.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weftlib/stamp.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#>   weftlib/words.lua  (new: the weft filter for rmarkdown)
#> Wrote: _weft.yml, survey.Rmd, weft-check.lua, weft-output.lua, weft.lua, weftlib/cond.lua, weftlib/config.lua, weftlib/ledger.lua, weftlib/lines.lua, weftlib/num.lua, weftlib/report.lua, weftlib/stamp.lua, weftlib/words.lua
list.files(dir, all.files = TRUE)
#> [1] "."               ".."              "_weft.yml"       "survey.Rmd"     
#> [5] "weft-check.lua"  "weft-output.lua" "weft.lua"        "weftlib"        
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
